newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Bahrain condemns Qatar's coup bid accusations.
newsitem.headline: Bahrain condemns Qatar's coup bid accusations.

text.p: Bahrain on Monday denounced Qatar's accusations that it had participated in a failed coup attempt in Qatar in Febraury.
"Bahrain regrets and condemns fallacies and fabrications by the Qatari foreign minister in his news conference in Doha," Cabinet Affairs and Information Minister Mohammad Ibrahim al-Mutawae said.

"It was a dangerous precedent that a foreign minister, whose country is the current chairman of the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC), uses the news conference...to attack another council member," Mutawae said.
Qatar's Foreign Minister Sheikh Hamad bin Jassim bin Jabr al-Thani told a news conference in Doha hours after a GCC summit ended on Monday:
"They (Bahrain) participated in the coup under the leadership of the crown prince (Sheikh Hamad bin Isa al-Khalifa)."
Bahrain "was the centre for the conspiracy...(smuggling) the weapons and explosives" into Qatar, he added.

"Until now he (Bahrain's crown prince) is continuing in the plotting...it is not for free. He is being paid for it," said the Qatari minister in Doha's first official accusation of Bahraini involvement in the coup attempt.

Qatar said in February it had arrested 100 people in connection with an anti-government plot involving former bodyguards loyal to the deposed emir Sheikh Khalifa bin Hamad al-Thani, who was overthrown in a bloodless palace coup in 1995 by his son, the current Emir Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa al-Thani.
Mutawae said Bahrain would send a memorandum to the GCC secretariat on Monday complaining about Qatar's "provocations".
Bahrain and Qatar are locked in a decades-old dispute over a cluster of Gulf islands held by Bahrain and claimed by Doha.
Bahrain boycotted the Doha summit. Last week Bahrain put two Qataris on trial on spying charges.
